strengths: Teacher selection under limited compute is an important problem for practical language-model distillation. The GPT2 and Pythia sweeps provide useful empirical evidence that larger teachers do not always produce better students.

MINIMA receives broad evaluation across knowledge, reasoning, coding, and bilingual benchmarks. Table 4 reports improvements over the variant without distillation on all six benchmarks, supporting the practical value of the recipe.

The manuscript provides objectives, data mixtures, major training hyperparameters, hardware details, evaluation shot counts, and repository/checkpoint links. Ablations examine pruning strategy, teacher size, distillation, and teacher assistants.
weaknesses: The central law is not established by the experimental design. Students are separately pruned and initialized from their respective teachers (§3.2), so changing teacher size also changes pruning severity, inherited weights, and potentially student architecture. The observed optimum may characterize this particular pruning-and-recovery procedure. A teacher-size comparison holding student architecture and initialization fixed is needed to isolate the proposed capacity-gap effect.

Evidence for a precise, setting-independent ratio is insufficient. The fit T = 2.498S − 11.498 lacks a documented point-selection/interpolation procedure, fit diagnostics, and uncertainty estimates. Appendix B compares only the 90% and 100% checkpoints of the same OpenWebText runs, providing little evidence about robustness across substantially different data budgets. Comparing 7B and 13B teachers for one 3B student supports a local observation but does not establish the predicted optimum or validate linear scaling.

The compute-efficiency claim omits an incurred training stage. Appendix C describes adapting the 7B teacher for one epoch on the 126B-token mixture, while Table 7 charges approximately 4.0 × 10^9 TFLOPs for distillation alone. Using the paper's own 6ND approximation, adaptation adds approximately 5.3 × 10^9 TFLOPs, bringing the combined cost to approximately 9.3 × 10^9 before pruning, even excluding original teacher pretraining. Rumor-based estimates for Mistral and GPT4-dependent Phi training further weaken the claimed frontier. Consistent accounting and sensitivity analysis are necessary.

Important ablation details remain unclear: whether the 13B teacher received matched Chinese adaptation, the resulting student configurations, and the teacher-assistant training budget. These details affect whether differences can be attributed to teacher size. Run-to-run uncertainty is also absent, limiting confidence in small differences and the selected optimal ratio.

The instruction-following evaluation has reporting and interpretation problems. Appendix J does not specify the GPT4 version or response-order controls, and Appendix M omits human judgment counts and uncertainty around Elo rankings. Spearman correlation of 0.54 is incorrectly interpreted as 54% consistency. The qualitative assessment also calls Table 15's coding answer successful despite its incorrectly returning the first array when the second array is empty.

The 'impossible triangle' is motivated by the overheads of selected existing methods, which does not establish an unavoidable limitation. The practical model results are worthwhile, but the manuscript needs narrower claims, stronger controls, and corrected compute accounting before its central contribution supports a Findings recommendation.
